label: t1-reporter-crit
topic: Track 1 adversarial critique of the frozen design: threshold-steepness separability in RBS-variant repressor gates (Cello UCF libraries)
summary: I recomputed every number the designer reported from the Cello UCF files and the arithmetic is almost all right; the one error is a count (10 strict calibration pairs, not 9). The design problems are elsewhere. (1) The 'untouched' holdout Eco1C2G2T2 is not independent: 15 of its 18 gates carry the same names as Eco1C1G1T1 and 13 have identical cassette part lists, so at least 9 of its 13 RBS-only pairs are the SAME constructs as the calibration pairs, re-measured in 2019 in REU instead of RPU (no parameter is byte-identical, so it is a re-measurement, not a copy). It tests measurement reproducibility, not generalisation. (2) P5 is refuted by the data already on disk: the single 'genuine' yeast pair (LexA) has different OUTPUT promoters (pLexA1 vs pLexA2, different sequences), so it is not translation-initiation-only; the in-scope yeast count is 0, not 1. (3) P2 is redundant with P1 and weak: S>=6 is only stricter than dn<=0.25 when Kfold<2.83, 48 percent of between-repressor pairs (where n is unrelated) pass it, and the Kfold>=2 side condition was added after seeing that calibration pair B2/B3 has S=5.00. (4) P3's r>=0.80 bar is vacuous: my refit gives r=0.972, but a refit with 0.5 noise on n would still give median r=0.87, and the pair-level dn values are NOT reproduced (r=0.086 across the 10 pairs). (5) The 'pure translation along log-x' story is contradicted by the data: ymax differs up to 1.74x and ymin up to 5.5x within RBS-only pairs, while only n is tested. (6) P4 and P6 are post-hoc, ill-posed or near-certain and should be dropped or demoted. Only P1 (re-expressed per family and in standard-error units) can really fail and is worth freezing. Caveat: I have now seen the calibration refit (P3 internal holdout is spent) and the holdout's structure (gate names, cassettes, output names) but no holdout n, K, ymax or ymin value.
lay_summary: A cell can be given a dimmer or brighter volume knob for one protein by swapping a tiny piece of DNA. The plan says that this swap slides the cell's on/off switch point but does not change how sharp the switch is. I checked the plan's numbers against the public data and they mostly add up. But the 'fresh' data set kept back for testing is mostly the same DNA constructs measured again, so it is like grading a student on the same questions with a new pen. One claim about yeast is wrong because the two yeast constructs differ in another part as well. Two of the six predictions are so loose that they would pass almost no matter what, so I recommend dropping them and keeping a tighter version of the first.

findings.claim: Eco1C1G1T1 contains 10 strict RBS-only gate pairs (same repressor group, same output promoter, cassette part lists differing at exactly one RBS position), not the 9 the designer states; the dn list the designer itself gives has 10 entries.

All dn, Kfold and S values the designer reported for Eco1C1G1T1 (max dn 0.1587; six pairs with Kfold>=2 and S = 12.01, inf, 83.56, 60.24, 17.60, 17.85; median Kfold 4.267) and for the two seen libraries (933W 0.2124/2.696/6.74; Lambda 0.0755/3.755/25.28; P2 three pairs; yeast LexA 0.2604/2.325/4.68) reproduce exactly. 0.25/0.1587 = 1.575, matching the stated 'about 1.6x'.
findings.source: Own calculation s1_recompute.py on the three UCF files (Eco1C1G1T1, Eco2C1G5T1, SC1C1G1T1)
findings.value: all match to the printed precision

findings.claim: The Kfold>=2.0 side condition (iv) removes the only calibration pairs that would breach the S>=6 line: B2/B3 (Kfold 1.733, S=5.00) is excluded; unfiltered, the calibration minimum finite S is 5.00, below the proposed floor of 6.0. The designer disclosed choosing 2.0 after seeing the data.
findings.value: B2/B3 S=5.00, S2/S3 S=7.90, P2/P3 S=11.11 are the three kf<2 pairs; kf>=2 filter leaves 6 of 10

findings.claim: The designated holdout Eco1C2G2T2 is a 2019 re-characterisation of largely the SAME gate designs: 15 of 18 gate names are shared with Eco1C1G1T1 and 13 of 18 have an identical cassette part list. At least 9 of its 13 strict RBS-only pairs (BM3R1 x3, PhlF x3, SrpR S2-S4 x3) are the same constructs as calibration pairs. No shared gate has all four parameters exactly equal (0 of 15), so these are re-measurements, not copies. Header: same host strain, units REU not RPU, M9 medium.
findings.source: Structure-only reads, scripts s8_holdout_structure_only.py and s9_holdout_param_identity.py on https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CIDARLAB/Cello-v2-1-Core/main/library/constraints/Eco1C2G2T2.UCF.json (2610885 bytes, sha256 ac3f586d...1bc); header via range request
findings.value: 15/18 names shared; 13/18 identical cassettes; 0/15 parameter-identical; 13 strict RBS-only pairs
findings.evidence_quote: "organism": "Escherichia coli NEB 10-beta"; "signal_carrier_units": "REU"; header version "Eco1C2G2T2", date "Mon Jun 17 14:13:20 EDT 2019"

findings.claim: Consequence of the previous finding: P1/P2/P4 scored on Eco1C2G2T2 test replicate-measurement agreement of n and K for the same RBS variants, not whether the invariance generalises to new repressors or new RBS choices. The selection-bias risk the designer lists (variants chosen by the library authors because they behaved well) is shared by calibration and holdout, and is not reduced by the holdout.

P5 is false as stated: the one 'genuine' yeast pair is not translation-initiation-only. P1_LexA and P2_LexA have different OUTPUT promoters (pLexA1_a/pLexA1_b vs pLexA2_a/pLexA2_b, different DNA sequences of 113-115 nt) in addition to different Kozak parts. The cassette-only side condition never compares structure outputs. In-scope yeast pairs after an output-promoter check: 0, not 1.
findings.source: s6_yeast.py, s7_outputs.py on SC1C1G1T1.UCF.json (1744232 bytes, sha256 ec14df19...d180)
findings.evidence_quote: SC1C1G1T1 P1_LexA/P2_LexA outputs ['pLexA1_a', 'pLexA1_b'] vs ['pLexA2_a', 'pLexA2_b'] | same name: False | same sequence: False

findings.claim: All 15 E. coli strict pairs (10 calibration, 5 phage) do share the same output promoter, so the side condition is satisfied there; the same-output check is needed only for yeast. The designer's SrpR terminator observation is also correct: S1_SrpR uses ECK120019600 while S2-S4 use ECK120029600.
findings.evidence_quote: S1_SrpR ('RiboJ10', 'S1', 'SrpR', 'ECK120019600')  S2_SrpR ('RiboJ10', 'S2', 'SrpR', 'ECK120029600')

findings.claim: Yeast pairs with IDENTICAL cassettes still differ widely in fitted n (CI: 2.06 vs 3.08, dn 0.40; CI434: 3.86 vs 3.92) because the gates differ in output promoter. They are rightly out of scope, but they show that two nominally same-repressor yeast gates can differ in n by 40 percent when anything else changes, so no yeast number can be read as an RBS effect.

The 'pure translation along log-x' narrative in the design's one_paragraph is contradicted by the data it is tested on: within RBS-only pairs the fitted ymax differs by up to 1.74x (PhlF P1/P3), 2.38x (933W) and ymin by up to 3.0x in E. coli (QacR) and 5.5x in yeast. In the 10 calibration pairs 5 have a ymax ratio above 1.15 and 6 a ymin ratio of 2.0 or more. The frozen predictions test only n, and the proposed Lean theorem requires shared ymax, ymin AND n.
findings.value: calibration: 5/10 pairs ymax ratio >1.15; 6/10 ymin ratio >=2.0
findings.evidence_quote: Eco1C1G1T1 P1_PhlF/P3_PhlF ymax ratio 1.74 ymin ratio 2.00 kf 7.67 dn 0.049

findings.claim: The lemma 'equal n is EXACTLY equivalent to the two curves being log-translates' (design step 6) is only true when ymax and ymin are also equal. Equal n alone does not make two Hill curves log-translates. With shared ymax, ymin, n: y1(x*K1/K2) = ymin + (ymax-ymin)/(1+(x/K2)^n) = y2(x) (own algebra), and the empirical data above show ymax, ymin are not shared.
findings.evidence_quote: given two Hill transfer functions sharing ymax, ymin and n, the second is the first composed with a scaling of the input, y2(x) = y1(x * K1/K2)

findings.claim: P1 CAN fail against the right null. Taking pairs of gates from DIFFERENT repressors in Eco1C1G1T1 (n unrelated to RBS), 177 pairs, median dn 0.366, only 32.8 percent have dn<=0.25 and 46.3 percent exceed 0.40. With the P1 refutation rule, probability of refutation under that null is 0.897 (3 pairs), 0.960 (4), 0.994 (6), 1.000 (12). But under a calibration-like truth the rule never refutes (0.000) and under calibration+seen pooled pairs it falsely refutes 1.1 percent (3 pairs) to 17.0 percent (12 pairs): the false-alarm rate grows with the number of pairs.
findings.evidence_quote: cross-family pairs: 177, median dn 0.366, frac<=0.25: 0.328, frac<=0.1587: 0.203, frac>0.40: 0.463

findings.claim: P1 is not independent across pairs: a 3-gate family gives 3 correlated pairs and a 4-gate family 6. Counting pairs instead of families inflates the apparent sample; the Eco1C2G2T2 design has 13 pairs in only 4 families (PhlF 3, SrpR 6, BM3R1 3, AmeR 1) so 'two or more pairs fail' can be triggered by one bad gate (one outlier gate in SrpR with 5 members produces up to 4 failing pairs).
findings.evidence_quote: strict RBS-only pairs (same outputs): 13 gates: 18

findings.claim: P2 (S = log2(Kfold)/dn >= 6) is algebraically equivalent to dn <= log2(Kfold)/6, i.e. dn<=0.167 at Kfold=2, 0.220 at 2.5, 0.250 at 2.83, 0.333 at 4 and 0.500 at 8. It is stricter than P1 only for 2<=Kfold<2.83 and weaker than P1 for every larger Kfold, so it is largely redundant. Between-repressor pairs with Kfold>=2 (n unrelated) pass S>=6 in 48.1 percent of 108 cases (median S 5.45), and P2 refutes under that null only 53 percent (3 pairs) to 88 percent (8 pairs), weaker than P1.
findings.value: null pass fraction 0.481; P2 null power m=3 0.531, m=4 0.717, m=6 0.692, m=8 0.881
findings.evidence_quote: cross-family S (kf>=2): n=108, median 5.45, frac S>=6: 0.481

findings.claim: S is ill-conditioned: n is shipped to two significant figures in Eco1C1G1T1, so a shipped dn of 0.0000 has a rounding interval of [0, 0.029-0.036] and 0.1587 has [0.127, 0.191]. S = log2(Kfold)/dn is therefore infinite or arbitrary for 2 of 10 pairs, and the median of S is dominated by the rounding of n.

My log-space least-squares refit of Eco1C1G1T1 from the 12x250-bin cytometry histograms (per-level histogram median, 60 random starts, scipy 1.18.1) reproduces shipped n across the 20 gates at Pearson r = 0.972 (Spearman 0.934); the refit/shipped ratio lies between 0.76 and 1.15, so 0 gates fall outside a factor of 1.5; max refit dn over the 10 pairs is 0.1115 and none exceed 0.25. P3 as frozen would therefore PASS comfortably. Note this uses up P3 as a blind internal holdout.
findings.source: s3_refit.py and s4_refit_stats.py on Eco1C1G1T1.UCF.json cytometry tables
findings.evidence_quote: Pearson r (n refit vs shipped, 20 gates): 0.972 ... gates outside [1/1.5,1.5]: 0 ... max refit dn 0.1115; pairs >0.25: 0

findings.claim: P3's r>=0.80 bar is vacuous. Between-repressor spread of n is large (sd 0.84 over 20 gates), so even shipped n plus pure noise of sd 0.5 (19 percent of mean n) gives r = 0.872 median (5th percentile 0.779), and noise sd 1.0 still gives median 0.655. The relevant pair-level statistic does not reproduce: corr(shipped dn, refit dn) over the 10 pairs = 0.086, and the within-family correlation of centred n is 0.354.
findings.value: r(noise sd 0.5) median 0.872; pair-level r 0.086; within-family r 0.354
findings.evidence_quote: corr(ship dn, refit dn) over 10 pairs = 0.086

findings.claim: The shipped pair-to-pair n differences are within estimation noise: Jacobian standard errors of refit n are 0.03-0.24 (rms SE of a pair difference 0.258, about dn 0.098), the largest refit z for any of the 10 pairs is 1.90, and 0 of 10 exceed 2. Shipped dn rms is 0.091 against fit-noise rms dn 0.079. The data are consistent with true dn = 0 for every calibration pair. (SE from a local linearisation of 12 medians, so approximate.)
findings.value: max z 1.90; rms dn shipped 0.091; rms fit-SE of dn 0.079
findings.evidence_quote: max z refit = 1.90; pairs with z>2: 0 of 10

findings.claim: Detection power per pair is limited: with SE of a pair difference 0.258 and mean n 2.63, a true dn of 0.15 gives mean z 1.53 and only 32 percent chance of z>2; dn 0.25 gives 71 percent; dn 0.40 gives 98 percent. A bound of 0.25 is therefore a coarse test that cannot distinguish dn=0 from dn=0.15 pair by pair.

The cytometry-histogram bin axis is NOT on the shipped parameter scale, so the refit cannot recover ymax, ymin or K in shipped units. Fitted ymax is 3.7 times shipped on median (ship/fit ratio 0.12-0.40, not explained by the models' alpha parameter: correlation 0.111), and K_fit/K_ship has median 0.57 (0.42-1.49) though log K correlates at r=0.903. Kfold ordering within a pair reverses in 3 of 10 pairs (all with shipped Kfold<2). n is scale-free so P3 on n is unaffected, but a refit-based S or Kfold is not comparable with shipped values. I could not determine the cause.
findings.evidence_quote: K_fit/K_ship: median 0.57 min 0.42 max 1.49

findings.claim: The design's non-monotone-gate exclusion rule (step Day 2) as literally written would remove half the calibration data: the strict monotone-median criterion fails for 10 of 20 gates and leaves only 3 of 10 strict pairs with both gates monotone. Any exclusion rule needs a numeric noise tolerance fixed in advance.
findings.value: monotone gates 10/20; pairs with both monotone 3/10
findings.evidence_quote: gates with strictly monotone median: 10/20 ... strict pairs with both gates monotone: 3/10

findings.claim: P4's headline ordering (TetR 0.1587 < phage 0.2124 < yeast 0.2604) compares maxima over 10, 5 and 1 pairs from three libraries differing in host strain, year, lab pipeline and shipped precision (2 s.f. vs full precision). On the pairs themselves, a one-sided exact permutation test TetR(10 pairs) vs phage(5 pairs) on mean dn gives p = 136/3003 = 0.045, uncorrected for shared gates. Fold, library and precision are completely confounded; yeast contributes no pair after the output-promoter check.
findings.evidence_quote: TetR (n=10, mean 0.0731) vs phage (n=5, mean 0.1363): exact permutation one-sided p = 136/3003 = 0.0453

findings.claim: P4 as a holdout test is near-vacuous: P(max TetR dn in a new library > 0.2124) is 0.000 if new pairs are drawn from the calibration pool, and rises to 0.19 (3 pairs) / 0.34 (6) / 0.47 (9) / 0.56 (12) if drawn from calibration plus phage pairs. Its outcome depends mostly on the number of pairs, and since the holdout shares 9 pairs' constructs with calibration it mainly measures re-measurement noise.
findings.evidence_quote: P4 refutation (TetR max>0.2124) m=6: if TetR~calib pool 0.000 ; if TetR~calib+phage pool 0.338

findings.claim: P6 is near-certain and its threshold post hoc: the headers show different measurement units (Eco1C1G1T1 RPU vs Eco1C2G2T2 REU), so K values are not directly comparable by construction. Its threshold 4.333 is one of the calibration Kfold values; 'cross-library K ratio of a repressor' is undefined where a repressor has several RBS variants; and Eco2C1G3T1 contents are unverified (scout claim). It tests nothing about the law.
findings.source: Eco1C2G2T2 header (range request); design-reporter.json frozen_predictions P6
findings.evidence_quote: "signal_carrier_units": "REU"; Eco1C1G1T1: 'signal_carrier_units': 'RPUG'

findings.claim: Every threshold in the freeze was chosen after seeing data: 0.25 is placed between the calibration max 0.1587 and the seen-yeast value 0.2604; 6.0 is half of 12.01; Kfold>=2.0 was chosen after seeing both calibration and the seen libraries; 4.333 in P6 and 0.2124 in P4 are observed values. The designer discloses the Kfold choice and the seen libraries, but P1's 0.25 and P2's 6.0 are tuned using the library the designer calls 'calibration only'.
findings.evidence_quote: I chose 2.0 AFTER seeing both the calibration and the two seen libraries - a disclosed, not hidden, degree of freedom.

findings.claim: Lean registry check at law set 1.8.1 (read-only): lawsets/current.json names version 1.8.1; gene-regulatory-dynamics is still 1.0.0, status 'proposed' (lawset-1.8.1.json lines 184-189) with lean_ref.module = null; the 1.8.x changelog adds no Hill, repressor or reporter law. Repo-wide search for hill/cello/repressor/ultrasens finds only altitude-coupling, flying-fish audit and laws.json hits, none about gene circuits. The earlier law-mapper's conclusion (no Hill law) therefore still holds at 1.8.1 although it was derived at 1.6.0.
findings.evidence_quote: "law_id": "gene-regulatory-dynamics", "version": "1.0.0", "status": "proposed", "kind": "biological"

key_claims.claim: The Eco1C2G2T2 'holdout' is a re-measurement of largely the same constructs as the calibration library (15/18 gate names shared, 13/18 identical cassettes, 9+ of 13 pairs identical to calibration pairs), so it is not an independent test of generalisation.
The designer's reported numbers are correct apart from the pair count (10 not 9); the real defects are structural, not arithmetic.
key_claims.evidence_quote: S3_SrpR S4_SrpR ptype=rbs n=2.8/2.8 K=0.06/0.1 dn=0.0000 kf=1.667 S=inf

key_claims.claim: P5 is false: the yeast LexA pair differs in output promoter, so in-scope yeast pairs = 0; P2 is redundant with P1 and passes 48 percent of unrelated-n pairs; P3's r>=0.80 passes with r=0.972 and would also pass under heavy noise; only P1, restated per family in standard-error units, is a real test.
key_claims.evidence_quote: cross-family S (kf>=2): n=108, median 5.45, frac S>=6: 0.481

key_claims.claim: The data do not support a pure log-translation: ymax and ymin change within RBS-only pairs (ymax up to 1.74x, ymin up to 5.5x), and the pair-level n differences are within fitting noise (0 of 10 refit z > 2).
key_claims.evidence_quote: max z refit = 1.90; pairs with z>2: 0 of 10

recommendations: Re-label Eco1C2G2T2 honestly as a REPLICATE re-measurement of 15 shared constructs. Its best use is a pre-registered replicate test: for the 15 shared gates, compare n_new with n_old and K_new with K_old (scale-free quantities first). That gives the missing noise floor of shipped n, which should set the P1 bound instead of a bound chosen from 0.1587 and 0.2604. Freeze that analysis before any n or K value from Eco1C2G2T2 is read.

For a genuinely independent test use constructs not in calibration: the Eco1C2G2T2 gates not shared (C1_CymR, V1_VanR, F2_AmeR: 3 of 18 names are new) are too few; the phage library Eco2C1G5T1 has been seen. State the honest conclusion in advance: no independent RBS-only holdout with enough pairs exists in the shipped UCFs, so the law is supported at replicate level only until new data (for example Bth1C1G1T1, if gate-repressor identity can be recovered from its paper) is scored.

Keep P1 only, restated: unit of analysis = repressor family (4 in the holdout), statistic = z=|n_a-n_b|/sqrt(se_a^2+se_b^2) from the refit with bootstrap standard errors, refute if 2 or more families contain a pair with z>2.5 or any pair has dn>0.40 with z>2.5. Under H0 (equal n) with 13 pairs the chance of at least 2 pairs with z>2.5 is 0.011; per-pair power is 0.52 at true dn 0.25 and 0.94 at 0.40 (own normal approximation). Report that detection of dn below about 0.15 is not possible with these data.

Drop P2, P4, P5 and P6 as predictions. Keep P5's correction (in-scope yeast pairs = 0 after an output-promoter check) and P4's table as descriptive findings. Add the output-promoter equality to the side condition and compare the full structure, not only the cassette.

Rewrite P3 as a method result without a pass line, or set a bar that can fail (for example: within-family centred-n correlation >= 0.8 and refit z-scores computed from bootstrap SE, with a stated tolerance for non-monotone medians). Do not claim that agreement tests the biology: shipped n and refit n come from the same histograms. Note that my run has already unblinded P3, so any new P3 should use a different library or a different fit specification fixed before running.

Add the invariants the narrative needs or remove the narrative: either a prediction on ymax and ymin ratios (data show 5 of 10 calibration pairs with ymax ratio above 1.15 and 6 of 10 with ymin ratio at or above 2.0), or restate the law as 'n is preserved within noise; ymax, ymin and K are not'. Correct the Lean lemma statement to require shared ymax, ymin and n before 'iff log-translate'.
Fix the pair count (10 not 9) and report S only for pairs whose dn exceeds the rounding interval, or drop S entirely.
Registry: gene-regulatory-dynamics is unchanged at law set 1.8.1, so propose the successor against 1.8.1 (the earlier law-mapper worked from 1.6.0 and its conclusion stands).

glossary.plain: The short DNA stretch that sets how often the cell's protein-making machinery starts reading a gene; a stronger one means more protein.
A number saying how sharp an on/off switch is; a larger n means a steeper switch.
The input level at which the switch is halfway between off and on.
The size of the difference between two n values, as a fraction of their average.
How many times bigger the larger threshold is than the smaller one.
How many doublings of threshold shift one gets for each unit of change in steepness; made up by the designer.
Data kept unseen so that a prediction made beforehand can truly be tested.
A data file in which the Cello design software stores the measured parts and gates of a circuit library.
Relative promoter units and relative expression units: two scales used to compare gene activity with a reference.
Redoing the curve fitting from the raw measurements instead of trusting the published fitted numbers.
How many times larger a measured difference is than its estimated uncertainty.
The DNA switch that the repressor protein acts on; if it differs between two gates, they are not a clean comparison.

could_not_find: I did not read any n, K, ymax or ymin value from Eco1C2G2T2 (deliberately, to protect it as a test); so I cannot say whether the shared constructs give similar n on re-measurement, and I have not computed the actual P1 outcome there. I did read its header, gate names, groups, cassette part lists and output-promoter names, and counted exact parameter equality (0 of 15), which now taints any claim that it was 'not opened'.

I could not explain why the cytometry histogram bin axis is on a different scale from the shipped ymax, ymin and K (ship/fit ratio 0.12-0.40, not the models' alpha), nor why shipped K is about 1.75x the refit K; the Cello fitting code and the Nielsen supplement were not read.

The Jacobian standard errors on n are a local linear approximation from 12 histogram medians; I did not run the 1000-replicate bootstrap the designer proposed, so the z-scores and power numbers are approximate.
Eco2C1G3T1 and Bth1C1G1T1 were not downloaded; claims about them (six gates, gate names without repressor identity) remain unverified scout statements.
I did not compile or run any Lean; the registry statements come from reading lawset-1.8.1.json, CHANGELOG.md and the law file.
I did not verify DOI author lists (only titles, venues and dates via Crossref). Author names in the citations list for Ferrell and Ha are unverified background.
I could not determine whether the cassette comparison is also sufficient in the Bacteroides library, nor how many in-scope pairs a genuinely independent RBS-only library would contain.
The file D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/data/cello-ucf/tree.json was already present in the data folder when I started (not created by me); its provenance is unknown and I did not use it.
